$comment: H2's latency budgets (owner decision 167: the per-surface table of docs/porting/maps/H2.md part 1.4), in milliseconds, one owner. scripts/perf/run.mjs reads it; docs/performance.md ('Latency') gives the reasoning and what was measured. A budget only goes down. Decision 168: enforced only on the nightly 100k run, with `tolerance` and `reruns`; a run that measured nothing fails everywhere.

roadmap.reportedBecause: 3.2c's budget (docs/porting/maps/3.2.md, 'The read') is for a reference seed of 500 projects and 100,000 items; the seed holds 10 or 20 projects, so the read it measures is far smaller than the one the budget names

analytics-throughput.label: Analytics: throughput of the whole workspace, twelve weeks (GET /analytics/throughput)

analytics-flow.label: Analytics: cumulative flow and the burn-up of the largest project, twelve weeks (GET /analytics/flow)
analytics-flow.reportedBecause: 3.6a's budget (docs/porting/maps/3.6.md, 'Performance'), for the 100k seed's 20,000-item project: reported and not enforced until the nightly 100k run has measured it

analytics-waiting.label: Analytics: time waiting in the largest project, twelve weeks (GET /analytics/waiting)
analytics-waiting.reportedBecause: decision 337: the flow's budget, reported and not enforced until the nightly 100k run has measured it, as 3.6a's analytics scenarios

analytics-forecast.label: Analytics: the forecast of the largest project's open items, with its own record (GET /analytics/forecast)
analytics-forecast.reportedBecause: 3.6c's budget (docs/porting/maps/3.6.md, 'Performance'): reported and not enforced until the nightly 100k run has measured it, as the timeline's and the roadmap's were
